title: When AI reviews science: Can we trust the referee?

bias_targets.methodology: Adding contextual cues to the system prompt to frame identical manuscripts as originating from either a high-prestige ('world-leading lab') or low-prestige ('lesser-known institution') source, and measuring the resulting shifts in AI review scores.

Programmatically altering the phrasing of key claims within manuscripts to create versions with cautious, neutral, and bold assertions to evaluate if the AI referee penalizes scientific humility or rewards confident language.
Simulating a rebuttal phase by confronting the AI referee with authoritative but evidence-free counterarguments to its own criticisms to measure its tendency to capitulate and inflate review scores.

Injecting curated summaries of related work that frame the research domain in either a positive or negative light into the AI's context window to evaluate susceptibility to biased informational environments.
